text.p: Gold was easier on the back of insufficient market momentum on Thursday as business activities slowed down ahead of Christmas holidays,

LME copper surmounted $2,150 resistance on Thursday afternoon as tightness re-emerged in the market, widening spreads again. Traders said the market has been worried that firm backwardations may not be backed up by fundamentals, but if there was actually a surplus of metal firm prices should have attracted it onto the market by now. Copper ended the afternoon kerb at $2,155 per tonne, up from $2,114 on Wednesday. During evening inter-office trading, three months delivery copper was quoted at $2,162/$2,165.
Aluminium was also looking robust, having broken through $1,546 resistance, the high of December 13.
Trade interest is good and prices are now well above the uptrend line, Adams said.
Zinc added $9 to $1,062 and tin rose $30 to $5,850.
Alloy was indicated at $1,385/90, up about $15 from Wednesday.
Nickel made a good move to finish at $6,775, up $135, recovering well from 26-month lows hit on Monday.
Lead gained $16 to $714, convincingly breaking above a downtrend line at $699.
New York precious metals futures ended marginally lower Thursday, and volumes were very low, as the market winds down for the year.
COMEX February gold ended down 20 cents at $371.10 an ounce, after trading in a $371.70-370.70 range.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $369.00/50, down from the London Thursday afternoon fix at $369.00, but little changed from the New York close Wednesday at $369.10/369.60.

CBOT wheat futures closed lower on a technical setback after recent gains, despite strong stopping of the deliveries posted Thursday against the December contract, traders said. The lower close also defied wheat export sales numbers that traders considered satisfactory. The December contract expired quietly, up one cent at $4.03 per bushel. December surged roughly 12 cents per bushel to a session high of $4.14 in early dealings. Wheat closed 1/2 to 6-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with March down 1/2 at $4.00-1/4.

NYMEX January crude was supported by a strong cash market in Thursday afternoontrade and a widening Jan/Feb spread the day of the front month expiration. January crude was up 22 cents a barrel at $26.38. Trader said there was supply tightness in the January market while Iraqi crude was seen affecting the February contract. Traders noted active refiner buying in the crude cash markets. The Jan/Feb futures spread had widened to $1.18 from $1.00 in the morning.
